### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0aaad18fc052326bc78378ead5f7e789f64e072d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c784678cc703b7692ea30d6b2a786390ee608f78` — the merge of head `1e7ced88b8d69d66d21991e95e82bdef048fa153` into base `0aaad18fc052326bc78378ead5f7e789f64e072d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c784678cc703b7692ea30d6b2a786390ee608f78 && git checkout c784678cc703b7692ea30d6b2a786390ee608f78
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0aaad18fc052326bc78378ead5f7e789f64e072d 1e7ced88b8d69d66d21991e95e82bdef048fa153 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0aaad18fc052326bc78378ead5f7e789f64e072d && git merge --no-ff 1e7ced88b8d69d66d21991e95e82bdef048fa153

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0aaad18fc052326bc78378ead5f7e789f64e072d
```

Scope: docs/adr/0120-unique-scope-vocabulary-and-null-safe-tenant-uniqueness.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-batch-data.ts (`callerMayReadObject` :135-144 and its docblock, `runBatchDataLoop` `case 'upsert'` :370-457, `case 'create'`), packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts (`findArgsBase` :830-834, `findExisting` :907-932, `willUpdate` / `willCreate` :1499-1500), packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts (`persistence` option :236-265, the no-primary-key docblock :476-480), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts (`member_default` :612-640 no-wildcard note, the `owner_only_writes` floor and its `public_read_write` relief :1299-1310), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts (`object_crud` layer :2779-2801, `verdict: grants|denies`), examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/semantic-zoo.object.ts (`sharingModel: 'public_read_write'` :28), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.upsert-existence.test.ts (titles), packages/qa/dogfood/test/upsert-by-id-caller-read.dogfood.test.ts (both suites, on `origin/main` and at this head).

Read-only shape held: the diff at this head (`git diff origin/main...FETCH_HEAD`, three files), ADR-0120's 2026-11-01 amendment as merged by #28694, ruling 5985885287 (#21771), the record 6561724481 on #28721 (merged as `7b62f0a77`, on `main`), the head's check runs (53 runs at reading time: 23 success, 18 skipped, 12 in progress, 0 failure), the PR's one comment (docs-drift). Nothing built or run. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; `Implemented-by` is the branch. No claim line was posted by this reviewer: the record is dispatched by the PM seat, which holds the head.

Disclosure check (ruling 2026-10-29): the ADR note, the create-door clause, the fork-comment clause, the test header, the test titles and the PR body were read for any sentence describing how an earlier path could be abused. None found. The ADR note states contracts (match key, arm, answer) and names a commit; the test header names the principal class, the object and the grants each holds, and why the object was chosen (the floor's relief on `public_read_write`, no baseline grant), all as positions; the fork clause names the earlier fork's reachable arm and nothing about what that arm admitted; the PR body's ablation names which cases go red under a mutated fork, not what the mutated fork answered. The `HIDDEN` labels name grants and the OWD only.

### ① Derived judgments

No runtime code moves: the accept set and every public face of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` are unchanged (the one `.ts` hunk is inside a comment; the PR body's measurement that the clause's text has 0 hits in `dist/` against a positive control is consistent with a comment-only hunk). The judgments are therefore of the governed text against the code it describes, on `main`:

1. **"The by-id upsert matches on the row's `id`, read as the caller — the object-level read admission, then the caller's own read of that id, under the context its write runs with."** Right. `case 'upsert'` with `record.id`: `objectReadable ??= callerMayReadObject.call(this, object, context)` (the security service's `canReadObject` with the loop's context; `true` when the context is `undefined` or the method is absent), then `this.engine.findOne(object, { where: { id }, context })`; the write that follows uses the same `ctxOpt`. Inside the atomic arm the context is the transaction's.
2. **"A row the caller can read is matched and takes the update arm, where the engine still judges the write."** Right. `if (existing)` → `engine.update(object, data, { where: { id } , ...ctxOpt })`; the CRUD gate, the floor and the write-class RLS all still run there.
3. **"A row the caller cannot read ... takes the create arm: the same insert and the same row answer as `operation: 'create'` naming that `id`."** Right. The `else` arm is `engine.insert(object, { id: record.id, ...data }, { ...ctxOpt, onFieldsDropped })` with the same `omitInternalFieldsFromWriteResponse` and the same result shape as `case 'create'`; a thrown refusal or collision is enveloped by the same row builder as every other case. No code of the upsert's own.
4. **"Every fact above holds for that arm."** Holds, read with the scoping the sentence carries ("for that arm"): a fresh id lands as given (`201`-class row); a collision answers `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION` and writes nothing on a PK-enforcing store; hidden-in-own-organization and other-organization rows answer alike (dogfood: stock `showcase_inquiry` / `showcase_private_note` / `showcase_contact` and the walled cross-organization personas, all deep-equal to a batch create); what leaves is bounded by the id's unguessability. The third fact's "visible to the caller" limb is vacuous inside the arm (a visible row is matched, so it never reaches the create arm); the note's own preceding sentence and its first bullet already say so. Not a contradiction; wording note under ③.
5. **"A held `id` the caller cannot read meets the collision, never a match. Import `upsert` matches on the mapping's declared key fields; this door's match key is the `id` itself."** Right, and the dev's rephrasing of the #28721 record's "unlike import upsert" is the correct one. `import-runner.ts`: `findExisting` filters on the first `matchFields` key set whose fields are non-blank and calls `p.findData(findArgsBase(...))`, and `findArgsBase` spreads the caller's `context`, so import's match ALSO runs as the caller and an unreadable row is `'none'`; `willCreate = !willUpdate && (writeMode === 'insert' || writeMode === 'upsert')`, so import also creates on a caller-read miss (the amendment's existing parenthesis for import says exactly this). What separates the doors is the key the match runs on: the import's declared `matchFields` (which may or may not be `id`) versus this door's fixed `id`. The sentence as written holds for both doors.
6. **"A caller without the create grant gets the create's refusal instead, the same for a held `id` and for one that names no row."** Right. A caller with no `find` grant has `canReadObject` false (object admission asks the find grant), so no row read happens and every by-id row takes the insert arm; `engine.insert`'s CRUD gate refuses `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` ahead of the driver, so a held id and an unknown id answer identically, and nothing reaches the primary key. Pinned by the new `CREATE_REFUSED` row (held-id case: upsert deep-equals batch create, and the plain create's status/code; unknown-id case: same, nothing stored, and `held` deep-equals `ups`).
7. **"On `driver-memory` the create arm lands a second row with that `id` ... when that driver runs with persistence ... the duplicate is also written to that development store. Accepted as the same residual."** Right in substance: the driver declares no primary key (`memory-driver.ts` :476-480) and the amendment already records the duplicate for every create door; a persisted duplicate through the adapter is the residual the #28721 record flagged, now written down. The naming "a custom `persistenceAdapter`" is loose: the driver's public option is `persistence: 'file' | 'local' | 'auto' | false | { type, path, key, autoSaveIntervalMs, adapter }`; `persistenceAdapter` is the driver's private field, not an option an operator writes. Should-fix (1).
8. **Create-door list clause** — "`POST /data/:object/batch` with `operation: 'upsert'` for a row naming an `id` the caller cannot read or an `id` that names no row". Right and complete for the by-id shape (an id-less upsert row is a create with no caller-supplied id, outside the list's subject). It points at the dated note, which is where the two particulars live.
9. **Provenance** — "ruling record `5985885287` applied to the per-object batch `upsert` by commit `7b62f0a77`": `7b62f0a77` is #28721's merge commit, on `main`. The ruling's text ("on the write doors, a row the caller cannot read is a row that does not exist") is quoted faithfully. The two pin links resolve (`check-adr-links` and `Check Documentation Links` green).
10. **Amendment form and Status line** — the note is appended inside the existing 2026-11-01 amendment blockquote, in the same bold-headed dated form, with its ruling record and applying commit; the Status line's existing `Amended (2026-11-01 ...)` entry already routes a reader to "the note under the business-requirement matrix", of which this is the tail. The 2026-08-22 D4 amendment is precedent for a dated note that does not add a Status entry. Acceptable as is.
11. **Fork-comment clause** (`protocol-batch-data.ts` :404-409) — "and that fork could reach the update arm for a principal the caller-read rule now sends to the create arm". Accurate: the pre-#28721 fork chose on `probeRecord` existence, so every existing row took the update arm regardless of the caller's read; the current rule sends an unreadable row to the create arm. Neutral: it names an arm and a rule, no principal class, no admission, no landing. It closes should-fix 4 of 6561724481 as asked.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right. The diff touches `docs/adr/**` (prose, governed), `@objectstack/dogfood` (`"private": true`), and one comment inside a published package's source; nothing published changes (a comment is not in the built `dist/`, and the body's measurement agrees). No `Clause-②:` line in the PR body: correct for a diff that moves no accept set and publishes nothing; the at-tier review is owed by the governed path, which this record serves. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` green at the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; `Implemented-by` is the dev branch. No `open_questions` block; the body's "Acceptance notes" are each answered here.
- **Pin soundness (the edit-without-read class).** `showcase_semantic_zoo` declares `sharingModel: 'public_read_write'`; the platform's write floor `owner_only_writes` is relieved by "a `public_read_write` update" (default-permission-sets.ts :1299-1310), so on this object an edit grant reaches every row and the floor's domain is left — the right object for a class the floor would otherwise mask. `member_default` names no business object and carries no wildcard (#5491), and no showcase set names the object (`git grep showcase_semantic_zoo` over `examples/app-showcase/src` hits the object and its translations only), so the edit grant the test writes is the principal's only grant there. Non-vacuity is runtime-guarded, not assumed: the guard asserts `/security/explain` `object_crud` verdict `grants` on `update` and `denies` on `read` (the layer's exact vocabulary, explain-engine.ts :2800), the by-id GET `403`, and the create `201` / `403` by class. Reading grants through explain rather than through a by-id write is the sound choice: a write would itself drive the fork under test. The one thing the guard does not prove is that the floor is relieved on the object (an `update` CRUD grant says nothing about rows); that fact is read off `main` here and is what makes the held-id case go red under the ablation (an update arm the floor did not stop), which the ablation measured. Sound.
- **Ablation arithmetic.** 36 = 28 + 2 classes × 2 arms × 2 cases. Under an existence-probe fork: held-id cases of both new classes red (4: the edit-only class gets the update arm's success instead of the create's `403`, the edit+create class the update instead of `409`); the no-create class's unknown-id case red (2: its trailing `held` comparison); the with-create class's unknown-id case green (2: an unknown id inserts under either fork); the pre-existing hidden-row cases red (stock 3 personas × 2 arms = 6, walled 2 personas × 2 arms = 4). 6 new + 10 existing = 16 red, 20 green. Consistent with the body's claim.
- **The pin is not run by this PR's CI, by design.** `Dogfood Regression Gate (n/3)` has `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && != 'merge_group'`; it was skipped on this head and there is no push-event run for the sha. The evidence that the 8 new cases are green is the dev's local run (36/36 under the verify lock), as it was for #28721. Not a must-fix; the PM seat should read the first push or scheduled Dogfood Regression Gate that covers the landed sha. Should-fix (3).
- **Head check-runs** at reading time: 0 failures; `Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Lint` families still in progress. Landing check ② (all green) is the PM seat's at landing time.
- **Docs drift** (comment 6563356782): nothing listed; `content/docs/**` is prose face, lane ACCEPT.
- **`Local-runs: none`**: nothing was built, run or replayed; the ablation figures are judged by arithmetic against the test tables, not reproduced.

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/adr/0120` (the one `hits` file). The change holds against the code it cites: every contract sentence in the note is realized by `case 'upsert'` on `main` as traced in ① 1-6, the import contrast is realized by `import-runner.ts` as traced in ① 5, the driver residual by `memory-driver.ts`, and the two pins it names exist and pin what it says (the protocol seam battery's cases 1, 3 and 10; the dogfood held-id / unknown-id cases, stock and walled, atomic and not). First consumer: the fork itself, which already implements the text (the ADR records a landed decision, as its amendment form says), and `check-adr-links` / `check-adr-index` / `check-doc-anchors` as the gates that read the file. Execution plan: none owed; the should-fixes 2-4 of 6561724481 that this PR exists to close are closed (door listed with the persisted residual; pin by name; fork clause). Consistency with the existing amendment: the binding sentence ("no create door answers a collision on `id` differently by the visibility of the row that holds it") now covers this door, and the note adds no exception to it; ruling 5985885287 remains the reason an unreadable row is a create here, and the note says so in the ruling's words. Holds.
